title: Untrusted data reaching an interpreter as syntax rather than value

threat_model.actor: Any caller who can place a value anywhere the application later reads it, directly on a request or indirectly through storage, a queue, an import, or a webhook
threat_model.asset: The integrity of every statement the application hands to a query planner, shell, template engine, or expression evaluator
threat_model.trust_boundary: The point where a value stops being data and becomes part of the program the interpreter runs
threat_model.failure_mode: A value is concatenated into a statement, or the statement is assembled in one place and executed in another where the escaping context is different from the one assumed
threat_model.impact: The caller changes what the statement means: reading or writing outside the intended predicate, executing a command, or evaluating an expression the application never authored

required_evidence: The application composes a statement, command, or template that an interpreter later executes
At least one component of that statement originates outside the application's own source, whether from a request or from stored data

signals: Values are bound while identifiers, sort columns, table names, or operators are interpolated
A raw or fragment escape hatch exists beside the parameterized API
A dynamic WHERE clause is assembled by string joining before any binding happens
A request object is passed as a query filter without shape validation, so an operator key can be supplied
A caller-supplied string is compiled into a query expression or aggregation stage
A command is built as one string and executed with a shell rather than as an argument vector
A safe argument-vector path exists alongside a legacy branch that still builds a command line
An argument value begins with a character the tool treats as an option
A template is built by concatenation and then compiled, so the input becomes template source
An expression or rule string from configuration or storage is evaluated at runtime
A saved view stores a SQL fragment that a later read concatenates into a WHERE clause
A worker builds an argument vector on the primary path and a shell command line on a legacy preset branch

boundary.subject: the application as the sole author of the statement being executed
boundary.object: the statement, command, or template the interpreter receives
boundary.invariant: Every component of an executed statement is either written by the application or bound as a value that the interpreter cannot read as syntax

examples: Query with an interpolated ORDER BY or WHERE fragment
Stored procedure body built from a string
Filter object built from a request body
Aggregation pipeline stage from caller input
Argument value that can be read as an option flag
Template source assembled from user content
Server-side render of a caller-supplied layout
Rule or formula string evaluated at runtime
Deserialized expression tree executed by the application
Stored filter reused when a scheduled report runs
Imported record reused in a later query
Queue payload rendered into a command

signals: Trace each statement backwards to every component and label each as application-authored, bound, or external
Search for the escape hatch beside the safe API, because the parameterized call is rarely where the defect is
Follow stored values on the read path, not only on the write path, since the write is usually the safe half
State which parts of the statement are structural and confirm that each maps to a fixed literal rather than a sanitized string
Decide whether the escaping applied matches the context the value actually lands in, including nested contexts
Treat re-validation on read as a requirement rather than assuming stored data inherits the trust of the writer
Identify columns, queue payloads, and imported records whose contents are later used to build statements
Establish who can write into those stores, since a second-order path can start at a lower privilege than the read
Exercise the builder function alone on structural inputs and record what reaches the generated statement
Use a local database or a recording interpreter double and assert on the statement text, never on production data

steps: Confirm explicit authorization and use a local database or an interpreter double that records rather than executes
Establish a working benign control call first, so a later difference is attributable to the input and not the harness
Submit structural rather than destructive inputs and assert on the generated statement text
For a second-order path, write the value through the ordinary feature and trigger the later read that consumes it
Record the composed statement, the interpreter, and the reachable entrypoint without running destructive operations

false_positive_filters: Every interpolated component maps through an allowlist to a fixed literal the application authored
The value is bound as a parameter and the interpreter cannot read a bound value as syntax
The value is server-derived from a trusted record and no caller-controlled path reaches it
The builder is unreachable from any entrypoint, or is a test double that cannot execute in the deployed path
A database policy or a separate authorization layer constrains the statement's effect regardless of the injected predicate, which changes impact but not the defect
The interpreter is invoked without a shell and the value occupies its own argument, so no metacharacter can change the command

required_evidence: The composed statement showing which component is caller-influenced
A reachable path from the entrypoint to the interpreter call, including the storage hop for a second-order finding
A safe reproduction that changes the statement's meaning without a destructive payload
The defective invariant stated as a data-becoming-syntax failure, and what the changed statement actually achieves
refutation_tests: Re-read the call for a parameterized form that the surrounding string formatting disguises
Check whether the interpolated component is constrained to an allowlist earlier in the call chain
For a second-order candidate, establish that the value can actually be written by someone other than the reader
Confirm the process call really uses a shell before treating an argument value as command syntax

root_causes: Structural components of a statement cannot be bound, so they are interpolated with sanitization standing in for an allowlist
Stored data is treated as trusted on read because the write path was parameterized
A legacy or fallback branch survives beside the safe path and still assembles a command line
Escaping is applied for one context and the value lands in another
A request object is passed straight to a query API that accepts operators as keys

variant_strategy.result_contract: EXACT | VARIANT | REFUTED | BLOCKED; exact and variant matches remain hypotheses until verified

remediation.canonical_invariant: Bind every value and map every structural component through an allowlist to a literal the application authored, on the read path as well as the write path
patterns: Map sort columns, table names, and operators to fixed literals and reject anything unlisted
Store structured predicates rather than statement fragments, and compile them with the same validator on write and on read
Execute processes as an argument vector without a shell, and delete the legacy command-line branch rather than escaping it
Validate the shape of query filter objects so an operator key cannot arrive from a request body
Keep the parameterized API the only reachable path by removing or gating the raw escape hatch
Treat stored data as untrusted input at the point of reuse, regardless of who wrote it

assertions: The vulnerable saved-view variant concatenates a stored expression into the WHERE clause despite a fully parameterized write path
The remediated saved-view variant stores structured predicates and compiles them through the same allowlist on write and on read
The vulnerable worker reaches a shell command line through its legacy preset branch while its primary path uses an argument vector
The compensated worker keeps a process execution and a rendered command string yet passes every caller value as its own argument with no shell
Remediated variants still execute the legitimate query and the legitimate transcode, so the assertion distinguishes enforcement from refusal

calibration.notes: This pack has not completed a reproducible benchmark run and makes no precision or recall claim.

limitations: Interpreter behaviour differs by engine and version, so a fixture result does not transfer between database or shell implementations
Second-order paths cross process and time boundaries, and the writing entrypoint may live outside the reviewed repository
A statement whose meaning changes may still be constrained by database policies, which alters impact without removing the defect
Static tracing alone cannot establish reachability through queues, schedulers, or imports without evidence about the deployment
